messages:
Maya Patel: Heads up — AcmeDocs is blocked. Indexing pipeline started failing after last night’s embedding model rollout. Customers are seeing ingestion errors and docs are stuck in the backfill queue. Error from indexer logs: `vector size mismatch: expected 1024, got 1536`.
Maya Patel: Full log snippet:
```
ERROR indexer.pipeline 2025-11-12T03:45:12Z - failed to insert batch
vecdb_client.error: 400 Bad Request - schema_mismatch: embedding_dim_mismatch (expected=1024 got=1536)\nfailed_items: 48
```
Maya Patel: Ticket says they started seeing errors right after we flipped text-embed-3-large -> 1536 dims in hosted catalog around 03:10 UTC. Backfill keeps retrying and hitting rate limits.
Ryan Chen: Which model id/version was rolled? Is that the hosted default or a canary? :eyes:
Maya Patel: Hosted default. Code path shows deploy-bot pushed `embed/text-embed-3-large@v2` yesterday.
deploy-bot: note: deployed embed/text-embed-3-large@v2 to hosted (region: us-west2) at 2025-11-12T03:10:07Z — rolling 100% traffic
Luis Gomez: Looks like embedding dimension changed (we promoted a larger model). VecDB schema expects 1024. Two options: 1) re-embed old docs with the new model and migrate DB schema to 1536 (lots of work + backfill cost), or 2) re-run ingestion/backfill with the previous 1024-dim model for historical docs while letting new docs use 1536 (mixed schemas cause problems). We should avoid mixed dims in same index.
Maya Patel: The indexer currently rejects mismatched dims — we saw `400 schema_mismatch` on every batch and then we hit vecdb rate limits because backfill retries quickly.
Maya Patel: Example curl that fails from the indexer service when we try to upsert a 1536 vector into index expecting 1024:
```
curl -X POST https://vecdb.internal/indexes/acmedocs/upsert \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VECDB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"id":"doc-123","vector":[...1536 floats...]}'
# response 400 {"error":"schema_mismatch","expected":1024,"got":1536}
```
Anita (eng-platform): Immediate mitigation options:
- Quick patch: make the indexer pad/truncate vectors to 1024 on-the-fly to allow ingestion to continue (lossy, not ideal). This is a low-risk hotfix to unblock the customer.
- Rollback: revert hosted default to previous 1024-dim model while we plan a proper migration.
- Migration: change VecDB schema to 1536 and run a controlled backfill using throttling and batching.
Anita (eng-platform): If we choose migration, we need to schedule off-peak window and add circuit-breakers for rate limits. Also alert billing — the compute estimate for re-embedding ~2M docs is non-trivial.
Ryan Chen: Can you paste the indexer command you used to repro? Need exact flags so eng-runtime can test locally.
Maya Patel: Repro steps we used in staging (copied from support playbook):
```
# run indexer in dry-run mode on a sample bucket
docker run --rm \
  -e VECDB_TOKEN=$TOKEN \
  -e BATCH_SIZE=64 \
  -e PARALLELISM=8 \
  ghcr.io/redwood/indexer:stable --source s3://acme-backfill/sample --index acmedocs --dry-run=false
```
Maya Patel: Result: same `schema_mismatch` error, indexer retries, hits 429 from vecdb after ~5 retries per second.
vecdb-bot: automation: detected schema_conflict on index acmedocs — current schema: embedding_dim=1024; inbound vector_dim=1536. See: https://internal.vecdb/schemas/acmedocs
Luis Gomez: Short-term I think we should: 1) revert hosted default to previous 1024 embed model (rollback), 2) schedule a careful migration to 1536 for the index (plan: schema change + staged backfill), 3) open billing incident because customer-facing backfills/compute will spike.
Anita (eng-platform): I can prepare a hotfix PR that pads/truncates vectors at ingestion. It’s ~30 LOC. Downsides: semantic degradation. Upside: immediate unblock for customers while we choose a long-term plan.
Ryan Chen: Eng-runtime can also add exponential backoff and jitter to retries to avoid vecdb rate limits while backfill is scheduled.
Maya Patel: Customer update: told AcmeDocs we’re investigating and will provide ETA. They’re asking if we can prioritize rollback or hotfix.
Maya Patel: Requesting eng-ml decision: do we want to keep new 1536 model as hosted default? If yes — we must execute a migration plan ASAP.
Luis Gomez: My recommendation: keep 1536 in catalog (it’s better perf for embeddings), but revert default for hosted until migration tooling and backfill plan are ready. Then do migration in phases: test index schema change on a shadow index, run backfill job with throttling, validate quality, then swap aliases.
Anita (eng-platform): Action items I’ll take:
- PR for pad/truncate hotfix (owner: Anita) — ETA 2 hours
- Prepare migration runbook + backfill throttling config (owner: Anita/Luis) — ETA EOD
- Open billing ticket for potential compute spend (owner: Maya) — ETA 30m
Ryan Chen: Eng-runtime tasks:
- Add stricter client-side retry/backoff for indexer (owner: Ryan) — ETA 6 hours
- Smoke test rollback to previous model (owner: Ryan) — ETA 1 hour
Maya Patel: I’ll hold customer notif and queue an urgent support call if rollback is slower than the hotfix.
vecdb-bot: note: scheduled maintenance window recommended for schema change — suggested window: 2025-11-14T02:00-04:00 UTC
Maya Patel: Ok, let’s do hotfix to unblock and then plan full migration. Anyone object to that sequence? :thumbsup: for hotfix then migration.
Ryan Chen: +1
Luis Gomez: +1 — will start migration playbook drafting
Anita (eng-platform): Working on PR now, will post link when ready.
Maya Patel: Thanks all — I’ll update ticket and ping AcmeDocs with interim mitigation.
